q1.question: How long does the process usually take?
q1.answer: Immigration timelines are controlled by USCIS, the immigration courts, and federal circuit schedules — not by us. A realistic estimate depends on your specific case type, current backlogs at your venue, and the completeness of your evidence. During your free consultation we'll give you a concrete timeline based on what your case actually looks like.

q2.question: What happens if my case is denied?
q2.answer: A denial is rarely the end. Depending on the filing, you may have 30 days to file a motion to reopen, an appeal to the BIA, or — in some cases — a federal petition for review at the circuit court. We explain all your options, the costs, and the odds honestly.

q3.question: Can I work while my case is pending?
q3.answer: In many situations yes — through an Employment Authorization Document (EAD, Form I-765) tied to your underlying filing. Eligibility depends on the case type and filing date. We file the EAD as part of our case packages whenever it applies.

q4.question: Do you offer payment plans?
q4.answer: Yes. Flat fees make costs predictable, and every engagement we take on comes with a written payment plan that splits the fee into manageable installments. We bill in full transparency — no surprise charges.

q5.question: Is the first consultation really free?
q5.answer: Yes. Your free consultation is a 20–30 minute conversation with an intake specialist or attorney. We listen to your story, identify the legal issues, and tell you what we'd do. You leave with a plan whether you hire us or not.

q6.question: Can you help if I don't live in Florida?
q6.answer: Yes. We represent clients in immigration courts and USCIS offices nationwide. Because immigration is federal law, your physical address does not limit who can represent you — most of our work is done remotely, with court appearances handled in person when required.
